draft.title: Non-linear structures
card: A linear story tells events in the order they happen. A non-linear story rearranges that order to shape how readers understand it.
In medias res
the story opens in the middle of the action. Readers are pulled in at once and must work out what led up to it.
Circular
the story ends where it began, such as with the same scene or line. This can show that nothing has changed, or that the character now sees it differently.
Time jumps
the story moves between past and present, or between different times. Readers link the pieces together and see how earlier events explain later ones.
draft.remember: Changing the order of events changes what readers notice, wonder about and understand.

a.q: A story opens with Jai hanging from a cliff edge, gripping a rope. Later chapters explain how he got there. Which structure is this?
opts: Starting in the middle of the action
A circular ending
A linear order of events
A jump between two time periods
a.why: The story opens at a tense moment and explains the earlier events afterwards, so it starts in the middle of the action. It is not linear, because linear stories begin with the first event in order.
a.clue: Where in the action does the story begin?

b.q: A novel opens with Lena locking her late grandmother's gate. It ends with Lena locking the same gate, but now smiling as she remembers her. What effect does this structure most likely have?
opts: It shows how Lena's view of the same moment has changed
It shows that Lena's life is exactly the same as before
It hides the events of the story from the reader
It makes the story easier to follow in time order
b.why: Ending where the story began lets readers compare the two scenes. The same action now means something different, so it shows a change in Lena. A circular ending does not always mean nothing has changed, so the second option is tempting but wrong here, as Lena is now smiling.
b.clue: Compare how Lena feels at the start with how she feels at the end.

a.best: Starting in the middle of the action
also_right: A jump between two time periods

b.best: It shows how Lena's view of the same moment has changed

problems.detail: The story opens in the present, then later chapters go back to explain how Jai got there. That fits the card's 'time jumps' (moving between past and present) as well as in medias res, so a careful student could defend 'A jump between two time periods'. Reword the stem or that option so only the opening position decides the answer, for example by asking how the story begins, or by making the distractor describe something the scenario does not show.

check.summary: Question a is ambiguous: an opening in the middle of the action that later chapters explain also moves between present and past, so 'A jump between two time periods' is defensible. The card, remember line and question b are fine.

a.q: A story opens with Jai hanging from a cliff edge, gripping a rope. Later chapters explain how he got there. Where in the events does the story begin?
opts: In the middle of the action
At the first event in time order
After the danger is over
Before any trouble has started
a.why: Jai is already in danger when the story opens, and the events that led there are explained later. So it begins in the middle of the action, called in medias res. It does not begin at the first event in time order, because how he reached the cliff happened before this scene.
a.clue: Has the trouble already started when we meet Jai?
